summary: PR #8 fixes a real app-to-app boundary, but it also introduces a report-only active lane that calls flags the target binary does not implement and creates a second hard-coded facet list instead of deleting the original duplicate.

findings.issue: New active lane `oya-governance-merge-queue-ref-hygiene` runs `oya-vcs-merge-queue-fix-loop-app -- --gc-staging-refs --max-age-seconds 3600`, but the app parser in this PR only accepts `--workspace-root`, `--initial-head-sha`, `--now-epoch`, and `--max-ticks`. `git grep` finds no implementation of `gc-staging-refs` outside the lane row. This lane is born broken.
findings.remediation: Implement the GC flags in the app and add a CLI regression test, or mark the lane planned/inactive until the command exists.

findings.issue: The new usecase crate duplicates the 21-facet panel while the dispatcher keeps its own `FacetId::full_panel_v23`. The comment says it mirrors the dispatcher list, which is exactly the double-bookkeeping the boundary fix should delete.
findings.remediation: Move the authoritative facet enum/list into the usecase crate and have the dispatcher import it. Keep one source of truth; delete the mirror test and duplicate enum.

findings.issue: The workspace-member parser hand-rolls TOML quoted-string extraction for inline arrays. It will drift on comments/escaping/multiline edge cases and duplicates what `cargo metadata` already knows.
findings.remediation: Use `cargo metadata` or an existing TOML parser path for workspace members; keep the gate about policy, not syntax scraping.

findings.issue: A focused architecture-boundary fix is mixed with registry/catalog rows, quality-lane changes, evidence, docs, and dispatcher dependency rewiring. The real product change is small; the PR makes it look larger and harder to revert.
findings.remediation: Separate the boundary/usecase crate change from unrelated lane/catalog/evidence edits unless the latter are required by a failing gate in the same slice.
